headline: Microsoft issues emergency fix for Windows Server crash bug
summary: Microsoft shipped an emergency hotpatch after an earlier update caused Windows Server 2025 crashes; outlets differ on which detail of the bug to highlight.

claims.statement: Microsoft released an emergency hotpatch to fix Windows Server 2025 crashes caused by an earlier update.

sources.quote: Microsoft has released an emergency hotpatch update to address Windows Server 2025 crashes
Microsoft hotpatches hotpatch that could crash Windows Server 2025

claims.statement: The crashes were triggered after installing this month's security hotpatch update, KB5131077.

sources.quote: triggered after installing this month's security hotpatch update (KB5131077)

claims.statement: Expiring IPv6 routes can bring affected systems down, and the fix does not require a restart.

sources.quote: Expiring IPv6 routes can bring affected systems down, though corrective update doesn't require a restart

discrepancies.explanation: theregister names expiring IPv6 routes as the crash trigger, a detail bleepingcomputer's text omits in favor of the KB number.

quotes.quote: Expiring IPv6 routes can bring affected systems down
Windows Server 2025 crashes triggered after installing this month's security hotpatch update (KB5131077)
